messages:
Jared - Polaris Health: Hi team, we're evaluating Redwood for a clinical note summarization model that will process PHI. We need a private deployment + BAA. What's the intake and eval process? We're aiming to go live in ~8 weeks. Thanks!
Nina (CSM): @Jared - welcome! :wave: We'll run this as a Private deployment. Can you confirm expected QPS, average doc size, and whether data will be in S3 or behind an EHR connector?
Jared - Polaris Health: Typical baseline ~2000 notes/day, peak ~5 qps. Avg note 3-5 pages, will come from S3 (we'll start with a de-identified pipeline, later move to full PHI).
Owen (Solutions Eng): We can support that. Private (VPC) + HSM/KMS for keys. Two deployment options: Dedicated GPU pools in our cloud region or an on-prem package. For 5 qps and 3-5k tokens per doc, recommended model family is med-summarizer-13b (quantized). We'll need to tune batching and KV cache. Do you need streaming responses?
Jared - Polaris Health: Streaming not required, synchronous responses are fine. Latency target: <3s per document end-to-end.
Owen (Solutions Eng): With those token lengths, <3s is tight but possible with proper quantization and 2x A10G or 1x A100 depending on throughput and concurrency. I'll draft a capacity/cost estimate and fallback configs (lower-precision quant or smaller model) to meet latency and cost goals. Also: what's your retention policy for logs and request payloads?
Jared - Polaris Health: Data retention: logs/audit for 365 days, payloads encrypted at rest. We also need export controls and strict RBAC.
Nina (CSM): Quick Q — do you want Redwood to run the safety/regression evals or will you provide an annotated eval set? We can do both; recommended is customer-provided clinical gold set + our safety checks.
Jared - Polaris Health: We'll provide ~300 annotated notes as a golden set and would like Redwood to run clinical accuracy, hallucination metrics, and the safety checks. Also need to confirm SOC2/BAA paperwork.
Priya (Safety Eng): On safety plan: we'll run PHI leakage detection, entity-level redaction vs pseudonymization, hallucination rate tests, and targeted prompt injection checks. We need a labeled golden set (~200-300 notes) and a schema for clinical labels (diagnosis, meds, plan accuracy). Also propose a hard-block policy: if output invents a new diagnosis not in source, mark as fail.
Jared - Polaris Health: Can do. Also prefer entity masking + pseudonymization for names; token-level redaction only for SSNs/IDs.
CS Bot: Intake ticket created: CS-2026-2241. Secure links and onboarding checklist have been attached to the ticket. https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/CS-2026-2241
Nina (CSM): Next steps: 1) Upload sample zip to the secure S3 share (instructions in ticket). 2) Fill the security checklist in the ticket. 3) We will schedule a technical kickoff with Owen & Priya. Is 10am PT tomorrow OK?
Jared - Polaris Health: 10am PT works for us, thanks :white_check_mark:
Owen (Solutions Eng): I'll prepare a preliminary infra sketch, cost ballpark, and a config that falls back to a quantized 8-bit variant to reduce cost if needed. I'll post artifacts to the ticket before the call.
Priya (Safety Eng): I'll draft the evaluation plan and send the required annotation template. Quick Q: do you need token-level redaction for PHI or is entity masking sufficient for your compliance?
Jared - Polaris Health: Entity masking + pseudonymization preferred. Token-level redaction only for numeric IDs (SSN, MRN).
Nina (CSM): Great — sending invite now and adding @legal for the BAA thread. We'll confirm timeline in the kickoff and aim for the 8-week target if the golden set and infra signoff happen this week.
